drivingQuestion: Does R' Meir concede that 'he did not die' is not a contradiction?
outcomeNote: קשיא: the difficulty against R' Yohanan is left standing (not a formal תיובתא)

segments.he: תְּנַן: עֵד אוֹמֵר ״מֵת״, וְעֵד אוֹמֵר ״לֹא מֵת״, אִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת ״מֵת״ וְאִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת ״לֹא מֵת״ — הֲרֵי זוֹ לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר — סְתָמָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קַשְׁיָא! קַשְׁיָא.
segments.en: The Gemara raises a difficulty with regard to this answer. «We learned» in the mishna: If one «witness says: He died, and» one «witness says: He did not die,» or if one «woman says: He died, and» another «woman says: He did not die, she may not marry. Granted, according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Elazar, the unattributed» statement in this mishna «is in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Meir,» that when a rebuttal contradicts the original testimony, one cannot rely upon the testimony that the husband died. «However, according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yoḥanan,» this is «difficult.» The Gemara answers: Yes, this is «difficult.»
